subject: Obs add-ons: retention windows, trace throughput tiers, and dashboard seat mapping
messages:
From: Lydia Chen <lydia@alphahealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-team@alphahealth.com
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on observability add-ons and pricing structure

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the dashboard and tracing features look promising for our platform team. Before we move deeper with a pilot, can you clarify a couple of pricing and packaging points so we can sketch internal costs?

1) Retention: we store a fair amount of high-cardinality telemetry. What are the practical breakpoints for retention (30/90/365 days) in terms of unit economics? Do you price retention by storage bytes, ingested spans, or by an approximate monthly cost per retained host?

2) Tracing throughput: your model demo showed per-request spans and sampling. Do you bill traces by QPS, sampled spans, or by ingested spans per month? Are there burst allowances?

3) Advanced dashboards: our team needs role-based seat bundles for dashboards (view-only vs editor). Can seats be split between teams and scoped to projects without doubling the license cost?

4) Discounts / pilot credits: for a 3-month pilot (non-prod), would you consider a blended pilot rate or credits against the first committed term?

If easier, feel free to send a short attachment with the mapping and ballpark numbers; we just need something to present to procurement and engineering.

Best,
Lydia Chen
Director, Platform
Alpha Health

---
(Attachment: alpha-demo-screencap.png)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia@alphahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on observability add-ons and pricing structure

Hi Lydia — great to hear from you and glad the demo helped. I pulled together notes below and looped in Ben (Sales) for commercial details and Rishi (Solutions) for technical sizing. High-level answers first, then specifics.

High level: retention is priced primarily by retained data volume (compressed bytes/month) with optional host-based cushions for predictable pricing. Tracing billing is by ingested spans with separate sampling tiers; we offer a small burst buffer for sudden spikes. Seat bundles are flexible — view/editor roles can be mixed within a single bundle with project scoping.

Details:
- Retention breakpoints: 30/90/365 days are supported. Pricing tiers: 0–5TB, 5–50TB, 50+TB (monthly retained compressed bytes). We can map host counts into those tiers for planning.
- Tracing: base plan covers up to X sampled spans per minute; above that we charge per million ingested spans. We use sampling policies to limit costs while preserving fidelity for critical paths.
- Dashboard seats: bundles can be split across teams and assigned to projects without seat duplication; editors consume an "editor seat", viewers a "viewer seat". We can offer a mixed-seat bundle.
- Pilot credits: we typically provide a modest pilot credit pool and discounted pilot rates that can be applied against an initial 12-month commit. Ben will suggest numbers.

I'll attach a short pricing sheet and a simple mapping example for Alpha Health so you can show procurement. Let us know which retention window and expected monthly spans you want us to size against.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(Attachments: obs-addons-pricing-sheet.xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia@alphahealth.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Questions on observability add-ons and pricing structure

Hi Lydia — thanks for the good questions. Quick commercial framing and a couple of options depending on how Alpha Health wants to balance predictability vs flexibility. See attached proposal PDF for formatted numbers. Below is the simplified pick-list.

Option A — Predictable annual commit (recommended for production teams):
- Retention: 90 days; tiered commit at 20TB/month retained compressed bytes = $6,500/mo (annual commit). Includes 10% overage credit buffer.
- Tracing: Standard sampling tier up to 1M ingested spans/day; $1,200/mo for that tier; overages billed per million spans at $80/M.
- Dashboard seats: pack of 25 seats (10 editors, 15 viewers) = $2,500/mo.
- Enterprise add: role scoping and project-level seat assignments included.

Option B — Flexible pay-as-you-go pilot (3 months):
- Retention: pay by actual retained compressed bytes at $0.12/GB/month, capped at a soft limit we patrol together.
- Tracing: discounted ingest price during pilot: $60/M ingested spans.
- Seats: discounted pilot seats (up to 10 free view seats + 2 editors) as credits.

Discounts and credits:
- For a pilot that converts to an annual commit within 60 days of pilot end, we offer a one-time credit equal to 50% of pilot billings applied to month 1 of the annual commit.
- We can also provide a 10% volume discount for deals > $250k ARR.

Next steps: if you can confirm an expected monthly retained volume and a rough expected average spans/day (sampled), Rishi and I will produce a tight estimate and an SOW draft. Attaching the proposal and a short SOW template.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

(Attachments: Redwood_AlphaHealth_ObsProposal_v1.pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on observability add-ons and pricing structure

Hi Lydia — adding a few technical clarifications to help sizing. If you can share a day-in-the-life metric we can convert to compressed bytes and sampled spans:

- Retention sizing: we compress telemetry using delta encoding and columnar packing. Typical compression for high-cardinality traces/query logs is ~6–8x. So if you report raw daily ingest (GB/day), divide by 6 to estimate compressed retained bytes.
- Tracing: we charge on ingested spans after sampling. If you need near-100% fidelity on a subset of services, we recommend scoped "full-fidelity" tracing for those services and sampled tracing elsewhere. Give us target services and expected QPS to size.
- Burst behavior: our runtime includes a 2x short burst buffer (30 minutes) before we gate; bursts beyond that are charged at overage rates. For pilots we can temporarily expand the burst allowance to avoid throttling.
- Dashboards: dashboard storage (queries and snapshot caches) is lightweight compared to raw telemetry; that cost is rolled into the retention bucket unless you require long-term snapshot archives.

If you can send last 30 days of raw ingest (or just approximate hosts x logs/day and average spans per request), I will turn that into a one-page forensic estimate. Happy to sign an NDA if needed for any sample data.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few follow-ups and confirmations after reviewing the proposal:

- For pilot sizing let's assume raw ingest ~1.2TB/day across all telemetry sources (including traces + logs). If I apply the 6x compression you mentioned, that yields ~200GB/day compressed -> ~6TB retained for a 30-day window. Please size both 30 and 90 day retention for that footprint.
- On tracing: we expect ~2.5M requests/day across services, with an average of 5 spans/request. We will likely sample ~10% globally but keep full fidelity on two critical services that represent ~20% of traffic. Please include a scoped full-fidelity estimate and pilot rates.
- Seats: we'll take the pilot seat bundle (2 editors + 8 viewers) and evaluate usage patterns.
- Credits: we'd like the pilot-to-commit conversion credit; that would make the business case much easier to sell internally.

Can you get back with a short numeric estimate and an updated SOW by Friday? If so, I will schedule a procurement sync the following week.

Best,
Lydia
Director, Platform
Alpha Health
